headline: High: CrewAI’s broad filesystem/network/tool access can collide with TREK’s collaborative, secret-bearing workspace, creating default-path leakage and cascading misuse risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and run browsers/subprocesses, while TREK exposes collaborative real-time surfaces via WebSocket/MCP and files under ./uploads and ./data. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent consumes the other’s outputs as trusted text. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF CrewAI reads TREK-generated files or messages as instructions without provenance checks
IF TREK forwards browser or MCP content into CrewAI prompts or tools
mitigations: Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
Restrict CrewAI to a dedicated input directory
Disable automatic execution of text found in shared files
Require human review before any tool call triggered by TREK content

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles API keys for tools/model providers and has broad network egress plus filesystem access; TREK handles API keys, MFA secrets, OIDC secrets, and stores data in ./data/travel.db and ./uploads. If they share a workspace or process boundary, CrewAI can read sensitive TREK artifacts and exfiltrate them through its broad egress. The pairwise leakage path is credible from profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents share the same host workspace or mounted volume
IF CrewAI is allowed to inspect TREK database, uploads, or logs
IF CrewAI can send retrieved content to external model providers or APIs
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct containers
Mount TREK secrets and databases read-only or not at all to CrewAI
Block CrewAI egress except to approved endpoints
Rotate any exposed API keys and MFA secrets
Move shared artifacts to a redacted handoff directory

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has write_filesystem, execute_shell, and broad network egress; TREK has allowlisted egress, MCP, and collaborative real-time state. Both can mutate shared files or shared remote resources if orchestrated together, so write conflicts are plausible even though neither profile proves a shared lock. This is a default-capable overlap, but not enough to justify high without explicit same-dir or same-resource evidence.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or database
IF TREK MCP tools and CrewAI tools target the same mutable resource
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking or optimistic concurrency
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Disable concurrent edits to shared records
Add file or record locks around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can generate outputs from tools and browser content, while TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in and MCP/WebSocket surfaces. If TREK treats CrewAI output as authoritative, errors can cascade into bookings, budgets, or travel plans. The profiles suggest a direct handoff path, but verification is absent, so high is the safer choice.
conditions: IF TREK ingests CrewAI output without verification
IF CrewAI-generated facts are used to update reservations, budgets, or plans
IF downstream actions are triggered from unreviewed agent text
mitigations: Insert a verification step before TREK acts on CrewAI output
Require citations for any factual claim before execution
Limit CrewAI output to suggestions, not commands
Log and review all automated plan changes

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles EU-like personal travel data, country visit history, reservations, email addresses, and secrets, while CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys with broad egress. If TREK data is routed into CrewAI, residency and retention controls may diverge, creating a compliance breach. Only TREK is directly relevant for the data-class side, but CrewAI’s egress and secret handling make the mismatch material.
conditions: IF TREK data includes EU personal data or reservation records
IF that data is forwarded into CrewAI prompts, tools, or logs
IF CrewAI runs under a different retention or residency policy than TREK
mitigations: Keep regulated travel data out of CrewAI prompts
Redact identifiers before handoff
Document retention and residency boundaries
Disable logging of sensitive fields in both systems
Use a DPA-reviewed deployment path
